subject: Customer request: EU-only model tether + no-fallback for certified model
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam@zephyrhealth.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: EU-only model binding + no-fallback for certified model

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. One of our compliance reviewers flagged that the model we want to use for our regulated workflows needs to remain bound to an EU residency model variant and must not fall back to any other variant or region under any circumstances — this is part of our certification evidence.

Concretely, we're asking Redwood to:
- Pin the customer route to model: rwd-eu-certified-v2 (no automatic fallback)
- Ensure requests originate and process entirely in the EU region (data residency)
- Provide an audit trail showing that no fallback occurred for the last 30 days

Can you confirm whether that is feasible on hosted/Dedicated plans? If not, what combination of Dedicated + Private options would meet this requirement? We need to get a mutual action plan to present to our compliance team by next Wednesday (2028-09-10).

I've attached our EU security checklist for reference.

Best,
Sam Torres
Director, Platform Security
Zephyr Health

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: EU-only model binding + no-fallback for certified model

Thanks Priyom — quick security read:

- Residency: we can enforce EU-only processing for a route by pinning to eu-region capacity and applying network controls (VPC routing, regional placement).
- No-fallback promise: on Hosted we have automatic fallback policies for availability. Guaranteeing "no-fallback" increases risk of silent failures if the specific variant becomes unhealthy. For certification purposes, two options are viable:
  * Dedicated pool (reserved capacity in EU) + explicit routing policy that forbids fallbacks. With mandatory health checks and scheduled maintenance windows documented, we can produce audit logs showing model_id per request.
  * Private/VPC deployment in customer's tenancy (preferred for the strongest guarantee) — gives them full control over failover semantics and audit.
- Audit trail: we can expose per-request headers (x-redwood-model-id, x-redwood-region, request-id) and a time-range log export. Those are already in our observability platform but will need a retention SLA aligned with their certification window.

Risk mitigation (recommended):
- Add a secondary manual-runbook: if the pinned model degrades, an ops alert + manual change is triggered (instead of auto-fallback). That preserves availability while meeting the "no automatic fallback" requirement.
- Legal needs to sign off on the SLA carveout.

I'll volunteer to own the security checklist follow-up and to enumerate the required audit artifacts.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Lead, Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Sam Torres <sam@zephyrhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Sep 2028 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: EU-only model binding + no-fallback for certified model — ops plan

Summary and proposed ops commitment:

1) Pinning: We can create a customer route that only resolves to rwd-eu-certified-v2 instances in the EU shard. We'll add an explicit routing flag ("pin_model_id: true") to the route configuration.

2) No automatic fallback: At the routing plane we will disable automatic fallback for that route. In practice this means: if the target variant reports unhealthy, requests will receive a clear 503 and our runbook will be triggered. We'll also implement a soft health-check window and automatic alerting to expedite manual remediation.

3) Auditability: We'll provide a 30-day queryable log export showing timestamp, request-id, model_id, region, and outcome. We can deliver this as a one-off export and discuss longer retention for an add-on.

4) Capacity & SLO: To keep availability reasonable, we recommend a Dedicated EU pool to guarantee capacity. Without Dedicated, availability will be subject to Hosted capacity constraints (higher risk). I'll coordinate with Capacity to produce a minimal Dedicated sizing estimate — ETA 2 business days.

Open items:
- Legal: confirm acceptance of the manual-runbook compensation for fallback risk.
- Pricing: if they require Dedicated + extended log retention, finance needs to sign off on showback and contract language.

Next steps:
- Priyom: confirm whether Zephyr will accept Dedicated or wants Private deployment.
- Irene: please share the exact audit artifact format Zephyr needs (CSV schema).
- I'll create an ops runbook draft and staging plan (canary with 1% traffic for 48 hours) and post into REQ-8892.

Marcus Lin
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference
